structured_output.summary: The diff is a thin wrapper. It keeps the spec step comments, calls date::this_time_value (step 2 RequireInternalSlot and step 3) and date::to_date_string (step 4), and wraps the result with agent.string. Nothing is special-cased and no errors are swallowed. The one defect is observable: the merged path produces "-000001" for year -1 where DateString requires "-0001". The gate report shows negative-year.js still failing for that reason. The cause sits in the support helper that this diff delegates to, which is not part of the diff, so the wrapper's shape is right but the output for negative years is wrong.

problems.question: contradicts_spec
problems.issue: Step 4 (ToDateString -> DateString) returns the year in the wrong form for negative years. For tv representing year -1 the output is "-000001" but the spec's DateString requires yearSign "-" followed by ToZeroPaddedDecimalString(abs(yv), 4), i.e. "-0001" (negative-year.js sloppy and strict both fail with this). The padding is done in the crate::support::date::to_date_string helper that this line calls, not in the diff, but the merged function still returns a value that differs from the spec on that path.

structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Keep this thin shape: RequireInternalSlot via date::this_time_value, then to_date_string, then agent.string. Fix the year formatting for negative years so it matches DateString: yearSign is "-" when yv < 0, else "+" (and "+" only applies when yv is +0 or positive; for the 4-digit form, years above 9999 are not padded to 4 digits). The padded year must be abs(yv) zero-padded to at least 4 digits. Check whether the helper in crate::support::date already does this for positive years, and whether it is the helper that pads the negative year to 6 digits (that matches the ExtendedYear form used by toISOString, not toString). If the helper is wrong, fix it in the helper's own file if the ticket allows it, or write a local DateString in this file and say so. Confirm that negative-year.js passes under both sloppy and strict, and that the rest of built-ins/Date/prototype/toString/ still passes.
